verdict.rationale: Slate's quickstart shows a whole-codebase architecture review that produces an ARCH.md as a recommended task, and it ships a built-in deep-research program. This implies it can explore and explain a codebase on its own, but the docs never describe how it finds context without manual selection. Missing for 10: documented automatic codebase indexing or context retrieval, an explicit explanation that no manual file selection is needed, and independent or hands-on corroboration of codebase mapping quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the agent map and explain an entire unfamiliar codebase without manually selecting context files

citations.quote: Please review the architecture of my entire codebase creating an ARCH.md and then give me ways I can improve it.
Have slate in parallel deeply research your problem
